title: The ground you trust most will one day shake.
subtitle: The final earthquake that opens the Day
then: Ibn Abbas said it means the earth {trap}will move from beneath{/trap}. Ibn Kathir links it to the call: {idea}fear your Lord, the earthquake of the Hour is a terrible thing{/idea}. A man once asked the Prophet ﷺ for one comprehensive surah, and was taught this one.
now: You plan as if the floor under your life is permanent: the job, the house, the routine. Then a phone call at 2 a.m. and everything tilts. This verse says {idea}one day the whole earth will tilt{/idea}. Only what you built for Allah stays standing.
old: My life is on solid ground. Things will stay as they are.
new: Even the earth is held up only for a while. I build on what lasts.
try: Next time you feel the ground under your feet, say a quiet thank you to the One holding it still.

title: The earth gives back everything buried inside it.
subtitle: The dead and the treasure brought out
then: The earth will throw out its dead. In Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ said gold and silver will come out like columns. {trap}The one who cut his family ties will say: for this I cut them?{/trap} Then they will leave it, and {idea}no one will take anything{/idea}.
now: The inheritance fight. The brothers who stopped talking over a plot of land. The friend you dropped for a better-paid contact. Picture that same money lying on the ground and {trap}nobody bending to pick it up{/trap}.
old: This money is worth the fight.
new: One day I will see the treasure I fought for lying unwanted on the ground.
try: If there is a money dispute with a relative, take one step toward peace today, even just a call.

title: What is wrong with it? The cry of the shocked.
subtitle: The moment certainty collapses
then: Ibn Kathir says man will be {trap}baffled by its situation{/trap}, after it used to be stable and firm under his feet. The earth and the heavens will change, and then people {idea}will be presented before Allah, the One{/idea}.
now: You have stood in a hospital corridor saying what is happening? when news came out of nowhere. This verse lets you have that moment early, {idea}while there is still time to prepare{/idea}, so the shock on the Day is not your first thought about it.
old: I will deal with the big questions when they come.
new: Allah tells me now so I am not the one asking what happened.
try: Spend two minutes tonight thinking honestly about the Day. Then make one small plan for tomorrow.

title: The ground under your feet is a witness.
subtitle: The earth reports what was done on it
then: The Prophet ﷺ asked his companions: {idea}do you know what its news is?{/idea} He said it will {trap}testify about every servant, male and female{/trap}: he did such and such on such and such day.
now: The car park where you said something cruel. The office desk where you fudged the numbers. The prayer mat where you cried at 3 a.m. Each spot {idea}is keeping a record{/idea}, the bad and the beautiful.
old: If no one saw it, it is like it never happened.
new: The very floor I stand on will tell what happened there.
try: Pray two short rakahs today in a place you have never prayed before, so it can speak for you.

title: The earth speaks because its Lord tells it to.
subtitle: All creation obeys one command
then: Ibn Abbas said: {idea}its Lord will say to it, speak, so it will speak{/idea}. Mujahid said He commands it. The ground is not acting on its own. It is {reward}obeying your Lord{/reward}, and the verse says your Lord, close and personal.
now: You think of the earth as dirt, concrete, a lawn to mow. This verse says the same ground {idea}listens to Allah{/idea} and answers when He calls. You live on an obedient creation. You can obey too.
old: The world is just matter. It does not respond to anything.
new: The earth obeys its Lord the moment He speaks. My obedience can be that quick.
try: Next time you hear the adhan, stand up straight away, the way the earth answers its Lord.

title: Everyone walks out in groups to see their deeds.
subtitle: People sorted, then shown what they did
then: Ibn Kathir says they return from the place of Judgement {idea}in separate groups{/idea}: the miserable and the happy, those sent to Paradise and those sent to the Fire. They are shown their deeds {reward}to be rewarded for what they did{/reward}.
now: At school you were sorted by grades. At work by job title. Online by followers. On that Day {idea}the only sorting is by deeds{/idea}. Not your surname, not who you know.
old: Who I am and where I come from will count for something.
new: On that Day I am sorted only by what I did, so what I do today matters.
try: Look at your plan for tomorrow and add one deed you would be glad to be shown.

title: A speck of good will not be lost.
subtitle: No good deed is too small to count

row.title: will be seen
sub: by the one who did it

then: The Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}guard yourself from the Fire even with half a date{/reward}, even with a good word. He said never belittle a good act, even pouring water for someone or {idea}meeting your brother with a cheerful face{/idea}.
now: You hold the lift door. You text your mum back. You smile at the tired cashier. It feels like nothing. This verse says {reward}you will see every one of them again{/reward}. Nothing kind is wasted.
old: My small good deeds are too tiny to matter.
new: Allah keeps an atom's weight of good. I will meet every small kindness again.
try: Do three tiny good deeds today: a smile, a glass of water for someone, a kind word.

title: A speck of harm will not vanish either.
subtitle: The small sins we wave away
then: The Prophet ﷺ told A'ishah: {trap}beware of sins that are belittled{/trap}, for they will be taken account of. He compared them to travellers each bringing one stick, until the pile {trap}made a fire that burned all{/trap}.
now: The small lie on the timesheet. The snide comment in the group chat. The extra five minutes you keep claiming. None feel like a big deal. {idea}This verse asks you to look at the pile, not the stick.{/idea}
old: It is just a small thing. Nobody gets hurt.
new: Small things are counted too. I would rather stop at one stick than build a fire.
try: Pick one small habit you usually excuse and skip it today. Then ask Allah's forgiveness for the rest.
